content.text: Same bug in the Organization page's "suggest" route. Fix both with the AI SDK's `output: "array"` mode (it wraps the array in an object for the provider).

input.command: node -p "require('ai/package.json').version"; grep -c "output: \"array\"\|'array'" node_modules/ai/dist/index.d.ts; sed -n 10,16p lib/import/organization.ts | cut -c1-300; sed -n 20,35p app/api/money/organization/suggestions/route.ts

python - <<'EOF'
import re
p='lib/ai/agent-runtime.ts'; s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
s=s.replace('generateObject({ model, schema: modelSuggestionsSchema,','generateObject({ model, schema: z.object({ suggestions: modelSuggestionsSchema }),',1)
s=s.replace('owned.categories, suggestions.object);','owned.categories, suggestions.object.suggestions);',1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(s)
p='app/api/money/organization/suggestions/route.ts'; s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
s=s.replace('schema:organizationSuggestionsSchema,',"schema:z.object({suggestions:organizationSuggestionsSchema}),",1)
s=s.replace('baseline.proposals,result.object,','baseline.proposals,result.object.suggestions,',1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(s)
EOF

input.recap: Fixed and committed on main (0fd44ab): the categorizer's AI call was failing every time, so uncategorized rows were never filled in. Tests and lint pass. I haven't checked it with a real agent run yet, and nothing is pushed.

content.text:
The agent team already does what you described. The Categorizer read all 132 uncategorized rows in your last run, and anything it categorizes gets applied automatically. Those changes show up in Agents under "Decided automatically", each with an Undo link. It didn't change anything because **its AI call failed every time**. In the run log it gave up after about a second with "The model was slow or unavailable".

**Why it failed:** OpenAI only accepts a structured-output schema whose top level is an object. The Categorizer was sending one that was a list, so OpenAI rejected the request:

> `schema must be a JSON Schema of 'type: "object"', got 'type: "array"'`

The "Suggest" call on the Organization page had the same bug. The briefing writer kept working because it asks for plain text, not structured output.

**Fix:** both calls now send `{ suggestions: [...] }` instead of a bare list. I sent the new shape to `openai/gpt-4o-mini` through OpenRouter and it came back fine. `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass. It's committed on `main` as `0fd44ab`, not pushed.

**Not verified yet:** I haven't done a real agent run with the fix. My local `.env` has no OpenAI key, and the agent team's default model, `gpt-6-luna`, needs one.

**What to expect:** start a new agent team run. Each run asks the model about at most 40 descriptions it doesn't recognise, so with 132 rows you may need to run it two or three times to cover them all.

input.recap: I applied migration 202610190004 to your Supabase database, and the run budget ceiling there is now 200. Nothing has been pushed, and I haven't tried a real agent run with the change yet.

content.text:
I applied the migration to your Supabase database, and the database now allows up to 200 model calls per run.

How the Categorizer works now, whether you have 132 rows or 1,000:

1. **Reads everything:** it loads every uncategorized row, with no 300-row limit.
2. **Your own data first:** saved rules and your past transactions categorize whatever they can, with no model call.
3. **One question per merchant:** rows that share a description are grouped, so 1,000 rows might be only 150 different descriptions. It sends those to the model 50 at a time, and each answer is applied to every row with that description.
4. **It sizes its own budget:** the Categorizer counts the batches it needs, keeps one call for the briefing writer, and raises the run's limit to fit. The 200-call ceiling only guards against a runaway loop; it covers about 10,000 unique descriptions.
5. **Bad answers are dropped one at a time:** if the model gets one suggestion wrong, only that one is skipped instead of the whole batch.
6. **You see what it decided:** results are applied automatically and listed in Agents under "Decided automatically", each with an Undo link. Accepted results also save rules, so future imports get categorized without the model.

It stops early only if the model fails, and then the next run picks up the rows that are still uncategorized.

All three commits are on `main` and not pushed: `0fd44ab`, `61ca958` and `450cf6e`. Tests, lint and type-check pass. I haven't checked it with a real agent run yet. To try it, run the agent team in Agents and your 132 rows should all get a category in that one run.

content.text:
It's built, committed and pushed to `main` (`dc9f117`, which also carries the earlier agent fixes).

**How it works:** open a transaction that has a category. If other transactions with the same description are in a different category or have none, the drawer shows:

> 2 other transactions have this description but are not in Groceries. **[Put all 2 in Groceries]**

Clicking the button does three things:
- **Moves them:** every one of those transactions goes into that category, however many there are.
- **Saves a rule:** future imports and agent runs put that description in the same category without asking the model.
- **Records it for Undo:** it goes through the same audited review the agents use, so you can undo it from Money → Organization.

**What counts as the same description:** matching ignores capitals, punctuation, reference or invoice numbers, and prefixes like "Card payment". For example, "Netto Marken-Discount", "NETTO MARKEN-DISCOUNT" and "Card payment Netto Marken-Discount" all match. It goes by description only, not merchant. The banner doesn't appear on split transactions.

**How I checked it:** I added 3 look-alike transactions to the QA test user's workspace, categorized one and clicked the button. All three ended up in the category, the rule was saved, and the banner disappeared. I then emptied the QA workspace. Your own data wasn't touched. Tests and lint pass, and I added a small test for the matching.

The check used a headless browser with the saved QA session. The "Sign in instantly (local dev)" button on the login page didn't keep me signed in, which may be worth a look.
